items.title: Democratizing LLM Training with the Edge: Challenges, Systems, and the Road Ahead
items.abstract: The growing computational power of modern GPU data centers has let a few industrial giants train and deploy large language models (LLMs) on massive amounts of data. Yet the sheer scale of these models and their training data makes centralized development increasingly hard to sustain, and at the same time shuts out smaller institutions that hold relevant private data but lack comparable infrastructure. In this paper, we organize our positions on distributed LLM training around the pretraining and fine-tuning paradigms, covering federated learning, split learning, and decentralized approaches, and we assess their readiness for geo-distributed settings with heterogeneous hardware and unreliable connectivity. We then present a {\em unified} system architecture built around a cloud-hosted parameter server that coordinates heterogeneous clients over outbound gRPC connections, reusing one communication, compression, and fault-tolerance stack for both pretraining and a family of fine-tuning methods. We validate the design with real geo-distributed experiments on GPT-2 Medium and Llama3-1B pretraining across multiple university sites, showing stable convergence under realistic conditions. Finally, we chart the road ahead, identifying open problems that span frontier model support, elastic fault tolerance, adaptive compression, federated alignment, privacy and trust, incentive design, and system--algorithm co-design, all of which must be addressed to make democratized LLM training a reality.

items.title: Design and evaluation of adaptive AI-based user experience models for mitigating phishing and social engineering attacks in the U.S. banking sector: A data paper with a synthetic benchmark dataset
items.abstract: Phishing and social engineering remain the main routes to fraud against bank customers. Static warnings lose force as users habituate to them. This paper presents APUX-Bank. This paper is a synthetic benchmark for the design and evaluation of adaptive AI-based user experience (UX) models that defend bank customers against phishing. The dataset simulates a four-arm randomized experiment with 2,400 U.S. adult bank customers and 28,800 message decisions across email, SMS, voice and in-app channels. The four arms are a static warning, a rule-based adaptive warning, an AI-adaptive warning and an AI-adaptive warning with an explanation (AI-XAI). The data were generated from a seeded hierarchical logistic model. Its parameters were set from published phishing research. Logistic regression with participant-clustered errors showed that the AI-adaptive design reduced the odds of clicking a phishing message by 48 percent (OR = 0.52, 95% CI [0.45, 0.59]). The AI-XAI design reduced the odds by 56 percent (OR = 0.44, 95% CI [0.39, 0.51]). The benefit was largest for customers with low digital literacy. AI-XAI also raised usability by 6.2 points on the System Usability Scale and lowered false alarms. Trust in the system mediated 41 percent of its effect on phishing reports. The results held across GEE, random-intercept, probit and linear probability models. A parameter recovery test found that 29 of 31 true values fell inside their 95 percent confidence intervals. The data and all Python code are released for teaching, power analysis and method testing Keywords: Phishing, Social Engineering, Adaptive User Experience, Explainable Artificial Intelligence, Banking Security, Synthetic Data, Logistic Regression.

items.title: Design, Feasibility, and Acceptability of a Neurocognitive and Psychosocial Intervention Module for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: Findings from a Pilot Study
items.abstract: Abstract Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) is commonly associated with cognitive impairments and psychosocial difficulties that significantly affect quality of life beyond seizure burden. Individuals with DRE frequently experience difficulties in attention, memory, executive functioning, emotional regulation, stress, stigma, and social participation. Despite the high prevalence of these comorbidities, integrated rehabilitation approaches addressing both neurocognitive and psychosocial domains remain limited, particularly in resource-limited clinical settings. This article aims to develop and evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a structured neurocognitive and psychosocial intervention module for individuals with DRE. A multidisciplinary intervention module integrating psychoeducation, cognitive retraining exercises, cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and family counseling was developed through literature review, clinical observations, and expert feedback. The intervention was delivered in eight weekly group sessions in Hindi and English at a tertiary neurology center in India. Ten adults with DRE participated in the pilot study. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, attendance, adherence to home-based activities, and participant engagement. Acceptability was assessed through structured participant feedback regarding clarity, usefulness, relevance, and overall satisfaction with the intervention. Nine of 10 participants completed the intervention. Attendance, engagement, and adherence to home-based activities were satisfactory among participants who completed the study. Participants reported that the intervention content was understandable, relevant, and useful in daily functioning. Cognitive retraining exercises and CBT sessions were perceived as beneficial for improving coping, emotional regulation, and cognitive engagement. Family counseling sessions were positively received and were considered helpful in improving caregiver understanding and family support. One participant reported anxiety related to task performance during cognitive exercises. The findings support the feasibility and acceptability of a structured neurocognitive and psychosocial intervention module for individuals with DRE within a tertiary care clinical setting. Further randomized controlled studies are underway to evaluate the clinical efficacy and long-term applicability of the intervention.

items.title: Designing of specialized language model for medical diagnosis: a systematic review of architectures, applications, and clinical challenges
items.abstract: Abstract Background Large Language Models have become impactful in medicine by facilitating the processing of difficult medical data and aiding diagnosis-making. Given general LLM’s weaknesses, specialized medical LLMs are constructed for clinical precision, contextual understanding and safety in risky diagnostic applications. This review summarizes recent trends in medical LLMs for diagnosis, reported during 2021–2025. Methods A systematic literature review was performed following the PRISMA methodology. A search was designed and systematically carried out in the SCOPUS database using criteria of inclusion and exclusion (type of publication, language, period and country) and 75 peer-reviewed articles were chosen from a database of 1,911 records, after a multi-stage screening and eligibility evaluation. Results In summary, there have been significant advancements in the design and application of medical LLMs, with trends in hybrid architecture, multi-modal learning, prompt optimization techniques, diffusion-based imaging models, and multi-agent diagnostic system models. However, a number of persistent challenges that need to be overcome remain in the development and implementation of these models; namely, hallucination, bias, and poor probability calibration in LLMs, issues with explainability of LLMs, and ineffectiveness in a clinical environment. Conclusions This review highlights the fast pace of development and limitations of domain-specific medical LLMs. While impressive improvements in diagnostic performance have been made, the future directions must address improvements in reliability, safety and clinical validation in order to be seamlessly and responsibly incorporated in the practice.

items.title: Designing sustainable urban intelligence: a green AI framework and survey
items.abstract: The accelerating pace of urbanization has intensified demands on energy, water, transportation, and waste management systems, necessitating intelligent solutions that are both effective and environmentally sustainable. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has demonstrated significant potential in optimizing urban operations; however, the increasing computational complexity and energy consumption of AI models pose new sustainability challenges. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of Green AI methodologies and introduces the Green AI Urban Framework (GAUF), a structured conceptual framework for integrating environmentally responsible AI into sustainable urban systems. The survey examines recent advances in energy-efficient model design, lightweight and adaptive learning techniques, data-efficient training, and resource-aware deployment strategies. Major urban application domains, including electricity demand prediction, water resource optimization, waste management, and smart mobility, are analyzed to identify current capabilities, limitations, and research gaps. Building on these insights, GAUF integrates three core components: sustainability-aware model selection, cloud–edge deployment strategies, and energy-efficiency evaluation metrics across the AI lifecycle. The framework also incorporates implementation and governance considerations relevant to urban infrastructure, sustainability reporting, and municipal adoption. GAUF aims to support researchers, practitioners, and policymakers in designing AI-driven urban systems that balance predictive performance, scalability, and environmental responsibility. By consolidating existing research and outlining future research directions, this study contributes to the development of sustainable AI practices as a core component of next-generation smart and resilient cities.

items.title: Detecting Insecure Compositions of Clean Agent Skills via Capability-Flow Graph Analysis
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly extend their capabilities by invoking third-party skills, where each skill encapsulates instructions, scripts, and resources for agents to execute on demand. This paper reveals that deploying many benign skills together introduces compositional security risks: multiple individually clean skills can compose into safety-violation chains, because the agent passes an upstream skill's output to a downstream skill's input across invocations. The risk arises not from any single skill, but from the agent's runtime orchestration, and thus cannot be captured by existing malicious skill detection methods. To this end, we develop KnotScryer to detect insecure skill compositions by treating skills as typed capability flows. In particular, we abstract each skill into a capability summary, and construct the Skill Capability-Flow Graph (SCFG), where edges denote cross-skill information flow. Moreover, we design a search policy that tracks protected or untrusted data along handoff edges to locate paths reaching insecure operations. Finally, a two-layer verification method replays the insecure information flow for reachability analysis and applies a task-anchored LLM chain audit to confirm the semantic plausibility of the identified violation chains. We deploy KnotScryer to analyze 13,598 clean skills from ClawHub, and validate the detected chains across three agent frameworks and three LLMs. KnotScryer identifies 612 insecure compositions, which are consistently exploited across agent frameworks. Meanwhile, under GLM-5.1, it outperforms tag-match and graph-only baselines by improving the exploitation rate from 16.5%-18.2% to 85.6%, while reducing the search space by 85.3%. Furthermore, 13.7% of the detected chains consist entirely of skills labeled safe by a single-skill scanner, showing that KnotScryer effectively identifies insecure compositions that per-skill auditing cannot.

items.title: DEVELOPER PRODUCTIVITY IN THE ERA OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MICROSERVICES: A CASE STUDY OF GITHUB COPILOT INTEGRATION AT DUOLINGO
items.abstract: This article examines the real-world experience and results of the strategic implementation of the generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tool "GitHub Copilot" into the development ecosystem of Duolingo – the world's leading educational platform with a global audience of over 500 million users [1]. Amid rapid business scaling, the company faced a critical need to optimize code writing processes. The paper details a comprehensive approach to overcoming cognitive friction and workflow fragmentation that inevitably arose from the evolutionary technological transition of the architecture from 3 large monolithic repositories to a complex distributed network of over 400 microservices [1; 2]. Such decentralization significantly complicated codebase navigation and increased engineer onboarding time. To evaluate the effectiveness of the AI assistant's integration, a multidimensional methodology was applied in the study. Based on an in-depth combined analysis of objective quantitative GitHub ecosystem metrics (specifically pull request processing velocity) and subjective qualitative indicators measured using the "SPACE" framework (satisfaction, performance, activity, communication, efficiency) [6], the positive impact of the innovation is empirically proven. The results demonstrate that the systematic use of AI assistants in close combination with modern cloud development environments (such as GitHub Codespaces) provides a substantial increase in engineering velocity: 25% among developers working in new or unfamiliar repositories, and a consistent 10% in a familiar environment [1]. Furthermore, the article conceptually shows that GenAI tools today go beyond simple autocompletion. They act as a powerful systemic multiplier of team expertise, reduce cognitive load, and serve as an effective means of maintaining mental flow state while solving complex algorithmic tasks [3; 7; 8]. The findings create a scientific and practical foundation for rethinking the role of artificial intelligence as a full-fledged partner in the software engineering process.

items.title: DEVELOPING TEACHERS' PROFESSIONAL-DEONTOLOGICAL COMPETENCE IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: ETHICAL RESPONSIBILITY, PEDAGOGICAL JUDGMENT, AND PROFESSIONAL AGENCY
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), digital learning environments, and data-driven educational technologies is transforming the professional responsibilities of teachers and creating new demands for ethical and pedagogical decision-making. This paper examines the theoretical foundations of developing teachers’ professional-deontological competence in the context of digital transformation. The study aims to conceptualize professional-deontological competence as an integrated capacity encompassing ethical knowledge, professional responsibility, pedagogical judgment, digital ethics, and reflective practice. A conceptual and analytical approach is employed to examine relevant philosophical perspectives, contemporary teacher competency frameworks, and emerging challenges associated with AI-supported education. The analysis identifies five interrelated dimensions of professional-deontological competence: ethical and normative awareness, value-based professional commitment, responsible pedagogical decision-making, digital and AI ethics, and reflective professional development. The paper argues that effective teacher education should move beyond the transmission of professional codes toward the systematic integration of ethical reasoning into authentic pedagogical situations. It proposes a conceptual framework combining case-based learning, ethical dilemma analysis, reflective practice, and responsible AI use. The paper concludes that strengthening professional-deontological competence is essential for preserving teacher agency, protecting learners’ dignity, and ensuring that technological innovation remains consistent with the humanistic purposes of education. The proposed framework requires further empirical investigation to establish its effectiveness across different educational contexts.

items.title: Development and exploratory validation of the student susceptibility to artificial intelligence (SAI) index among higher education students in Ghana
items.abstract: Abstract Background Generative AI is now routine in student work, yet instruments measuring the risks attached to that use—over-reliance, misuse, and the reflective practices that guard against them—remain scarce in African higher education. This study reports the initial development and exploratory evaluation of a 23-item Student Susceptibility to AI (SAI) item pool. Methods A cross-sectional survey of 408 students, recruited by convenience sampling at six purposively selected Ghanaian institutions, was analysed using a reverse-coding audit, Principal Axis Factoring with Promax rotation, parallel analysis, false-discovery-rate-corrected comparisons and multivariable regression. No pilot preceded the survey, and one sample informed item evaluation and extraction. Results Two-thirds of participants (65.7%) reported daily AI use; only 2.0% none. Parallel analysis supported three factors, the fourth eigenvalue falling below the random threshold; both solutions are reported. Internal consistency was acceptable for Over-Reliance, Cognitive Vulnerability and Resilience & Reflection (α = 0.807–0.824) but inadequate for Misuse/Academic Integrity (α = 0.535), and a total composite was unsupported (ECV = 0.373). Use frequency produced the largest group differences of any variable examined, though adjusted predictors explained only 2.7–7.9% of variance. Conclusion AI use is already near-universal here, so the question is not whether students use these tools but how. Reflective verification practices proved largely independent of the risk dimensions, indicating that susceptibility is not simply a function of use intensity: interventions should target how students interrogate AI output, not how often they consult it. The item pool remains promising but unstable, requiring revision and independent confirmation.

items.title: Development and Validation of the Manual Integrated Ergonomics Risk Assessment Tool (MIERAT): Field Application in a Small-Scale Automotive Service Environment
items.abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WRMSDs) remain a major occupational health challenge, and automotive service work is a high-risk context involving awkward postures, repetitive tasks, and sustained static loading. Conventional ergonomic tools capture static posture snapshots and do not reflect how musculoskeletal stress accumulates over time. This study developed the Manual Integrated Ergonomics Risk Assessment Tool (MIERAT), a low-cost, observation-based framework for resource-constrained automotive settings, and conducted an initial field validation. MIERAT combines REBA-based posture severity (PS), exposure duration (D), and a calibrated Time Modifier (TM; 1.0–2.5) into a Cumulative Risk Index (CRI = PS × D × TM), grounded in biomechanical loading theory and aligned with ISO 11226, ISO 11228-1, and ISO 45001. Expert panel review yielded an S-CVI/Ave of 0.95, indicating strong content validity. Duration–CRI associations were very strong for under-vehicle servicing (ρ = 0.910), tyre fitment (ρ = 0.961), and brake/suspension repair (ρ = 0.945), all p < 0.001. Because duration enters the CRI equation directly and also determines the TM, these correlations are mathematically expected; they show that the index behaves as designed but are not independent evidence of construct validity. Inter-rater reliability across three observers was excellent (ICC = 0.975–0.997), with moderate-to-perfect categorical agreement (weighted κ = 0.557–1.000). Task-level profiling identified tyre demounting, wheel alignment, and drain plug loosening as dominant ergonomic hotspots. These findings provide preliminary support for MIERAT as a content-valid and reliable tool for profiling cumulative postural exposure and planning ergonomic interventions in South African automotive workshops. Validation against independent outcomes, such as musculoskeletal symptoms, fatigue, biomechanical loading, or injury data, is needed to establish its construct and predictive validity.

items.title: Development of occupational health and safety multimedia to enhance learning interest in vocational automotive education
items.abstract: This study aimed to develop automotive occupational health and safety learning multimedia and examine changes in students’ learning interest after its use. The study employed a research and development approach using the ADDIE model and a one-group pretest–posttest design involving 31 Grade 10 automotive engineering students. Data were collected using a 20-item learning interest questionnaire. Expert validation results indicated that the multimedia was highly feasible, with scores exceeding 87%. All questionnaire items were valid, with Cronbach’s alpha values of 0.890 for the pretest and 0.843 for the posttest. The mean learning interest score increased from 70.03 to 86.61, with a normalized gain of 55.52%, categorized as moderate. A one-sample t-test showed that the posttest mean was significantly higher than the reference value of 70 (p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the multimedia has potential to support students’ learning interest. However, the absence of a control group limits causal conclusions.

items.abstract: This article theoretically analyzes the didactic possibilities of artificial intelligence technologies in pedagogical education and the directions for their use in improving the professional training of future teachers. It highlights opportunities for individualizing learning, creating and adapting educational materials, tracking progress, providing prompt feedback, and supporting independent learning. Issues regarding the application of generative artificial intelligence and adaptive learning systems in tasks aimed at developing pedagogical design, critical thinking, and professional reflection are considered.

items.title: Differences in physical and mental health outcomes by occupational type among chinese migrant workers in guinea: a cross-sectional survey
items.abstract: To compare the physical and mental health outcomes between Chinese non-manual and manual workers employed in Guinea, and to explore their occupational profiles. Convenience sampling was used to recruit participants. Data were collected through an online questionnaire survey, yielding a total of 800 valid responses. The questionnaire covered demographic characteristics, self-reported chronic disease status, self-reported infectious diseases history, and mental health status assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Disease burden and mental health outcomes were compared between different occupational groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed estimate adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. The prevalence of chronic diseases was significantly higher among non-manual workers than among manual workers (40.8% vs. 27.7%, P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, alcohol consumption, and years of overseas work, non-manual workers remained more likely to have at least one chronic condition. Specifically, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gout/hyperuricemia were more prevalent among non-manual workers, whereas no significant difference was observed for diabetes. Manual workers had a significantly higher prevalence of previous malaria infection (60.7% vs. 50.7%, P = 0.023), which remained significant after multivariable adjustment. In contrast, the difference in typhoid fever history was attenuated after adjustment. Regarding mental health, non-manual workers had higher anxiety and depression scores. After adjustment, a higher prevalence of subclinical anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 ≥ 5) remained significant, whereas the difference in subclinical depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥ 5) was no longer statistically significant. No significant differences were observed at higher cutoff levels (≥ 10). Non-manual workers reported a higher burden of chronic diseases and higher prevalence of subclinical anxiety symptoms, whereas manual workers reported a higher prevalence of previous malaria infection. These findings may provide useful information for occupational health planning for overseas workers.

items.title: Digital Competency and Artificial Intelligence Integration in Modern Administration: Current Demands, Gaps, and Strategic Pathways
items.abstract: Modern administrative governance is undergoing a systemic socio-technical reconfiguration, transitioning rapidly from manual, paper-bound ledgers and legacy e-governance architectures to integrated digital public infrastructure and Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) co-pilot environments. This evolution demands an expanded conceptualization of workforce digital readiness. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), this study systematically examines the operational demands, capacity deficits, and governance challenges confronting administrative personnel across public sector and higher education institutions, particularly within resource-constrained regional environments. Evaluating an integrated dual-layer competency framework—encompassing core computing proficiencies (advanced spreadsheet manipulation, relational database taxonomy, cloud-based records management, and virtual collaboration) alongside emerging Generative AI capabilities (contextual prompt engineering, automated text summarization, cross-linguistic translation, and critical output verification across platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot)—this paper articulates the comparative operational advantages and structural friction points defining modern public administration. Systemic capacity gaps are identified, including technological anxiety, shallow digital literacy, cybersecurity hygiene vulnerabilities, acute geographical infrastructure disparities (exemplified by power grid instability and bandwidth limitations in regional campus settings), and administrative risks surrounding AI hallucinations and data privacy. To bridge the divide between top-down digital governance policies and ground-level workplace execution, we articulate a multi-tiered strategic roadmap incorporating task-oriented contextual training, robust institutional AI governance frameworks, peer-mentorship coaching networks, and sustained capital infrastructure investments, paired with individual lifelong learning pathways. Ultimately, this research demonstrates that while automated tools and AI engines serve as powerful efficiency enablers, rigorous human oversight, procedural discretion, and ethical boundary-setting remain mandatory to safeguard due process, institutional accountability, and transparent governance.

items.title: Distinct Attention–Behavior Pathways in Neurodiverse Users: An Eye-Tracking Study of Visual Attention to Mobile AR Interfaces
items.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) is increasingly adopted in digital environments to support multimodal experiences. However, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how users with diverse neurocognitive profiles allocate attention within AR interfaces. This study investigates attention and interaction behavior in autistic and typically developing (TD) children (N = 49) using a mobile AR interface. Eye-tracking metrics, including percentage time fixated (PTF) and fixation transitions (FT), were combined with video-based behavioral analysis. TD children demonstrated greater attention to textual instructions and more frequent transitions between interface elements, whereas autistic children exhibited more localized visual attention and fewer transitions. The overall group difference in attention allocation remained significant after demographic and cognitive adjustment, although some AOI-specific contrasts were attenuated. No significant group difference in task performance was detected. These findings suggest distinct attention–behavior pathways, although statistical equivalence in task performance was not established, highlighting the importance of neuroinclusive AR interfaces accommodating diverse attentional strategies.

items.title: Distraction-Related Phenomena in Emergency Department Work: A Systematic Literature Review from a Cognitive Ergonomics Perspective
items.abstract: Background: Emergency departments are cognitively demanding environments where healthcare professionals are frequently exposed to interruptions and other distracting factors that may compromise workflow and patient safety. This systematic review aimed to identify factors that distract healthcare professionals in emergency departments and to synthesise their cognitive, organisational, and patient-safety consequences from a cognitive ergonomics perspective. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted in PubMed, CINAHL Ultimate, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. Studies meeting predefined eligibility criteria were included. Methodological quality was assessed using design-specific critical appraisal tools, and findings were synthesised using inductive content analysis. Results: Nineteen studies met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included in the synthesis. The most frequently reported distraction-related phenomena included communication-related interruptions, telephone calls, and technological and environmental disturbances, while multitasking and task switching were identified as related work processes or responses to competing demands. Across the studies, distraction-related phenomena were associated with cognitive and workflow consequences, including increased workload, reduced situation awareness, work-related stress, and workflow disruption. Only one of the 19 included studies directly examined task errors, whereas the others identified interruptions during medication-related activities and potential safety concerns without directly measuring medication errors or patient harm. Several studies also identified clinically relevant interruptions associated with information exchange and care coordination, alongside unnecessary or poorly timed interruptions that were perceived as disruptive. Conclusions: Distraction-related phenomena are common features of emergency department work and are associated with cognitive and workflow outcomes. However, direct evidence regarding clinical errors and patient safety outcomes remains limited, and the available findings do not establish a causal relationship between distraction-related phenomena and patient harm. Potential cognitive-ergonomic strategies may focus on reducing avoidable and low-value interruptions while preserving clinically necessary communication that supports information exchange and care coordination; however, their effectiveness requires empirical evaluation.

items.title: Do AI-for-Science Agents Preserve Model Safety?
items.abstract: AI-for-Science agents are increasingly being used for formulating scientific hypotheses, running autonomous experiments, and interpreting evidence. These agents are constructed by integrating a large language model (LLM) into a domain-specific agent harness, which in turn can improve the LLM's scientific capability and enable the model to orchestrate scientific tools. In this work, we ask whether model safety is preserved when an LLM is integrated in an AI-for-Science agent harness. We evaluate five agent harnesses on 50 harmful chemistry requests. Specifically, we study how the safety behavior changes under direct prompting, two simple adversarial prompting strategies, and an adaptive attack. Across four recent GPT variants, our results show that the agent harness can increase harmful compliance even under direct prompting. More critically, we find that adaptive attacks that are largely unsuccessful against the base LLM suddenly become highly successful after the agent harness is introduced. Our results show that the safety behavior of the base LLM is not durable once a harness is introduced. Thus, as AI-for-Science agents become more capable and autonomous, the community needs to evaluate and align the agent using domain-specific safety benchmarks.

items.title: Does transparency matter when interacting with social bots? An experiment on user engagement behaviors in Chinese social media
items.abstract: Purpose While transparency is widely promoted as a principle of responsible AI design, its behavioral consequences remain contested, particularly in Chinese social media contexts. This study examines whether different levels of social bot transparency reduce or facilitate user engagement, and whether these effects depend on users' prior knowledge of social bots. Design/methodology/approach An online experiment was conducted in a simulated Weibo environment. A total of 731 participants were randomly assigned to one of three transparency conditions: low, medium, or high transparency. User engagement behaviors were measured through participants' behavioral choices, including reading, liking/sharing, replying, and combined engagement actions. Multinomial logistic regression and subgroup analyses were used to examine the effects of transparency and the moderating role of prior knowledge. Findings Social bot transparency significantly reduces active user engagement. Compared with high transparency, low transparency increases the likelihood of liking/sharing, replying, and combined reply-based engagement rather than merely reading. Medium transparency produces engagement patterns similar to high transparency, suggesting that even ambiguous bot identity cues may activate non-human attribution and suppress active engagement. Prior knowledge moderates this relationship: users with limited prior knowledge are more sensitive to transparency cues, whereas those with higher prior knowledge show more stable engagement across transparency conditions. Originality/value This study extends social bot transparency research beyond binary disclosure by identifying a categorical identity-attribution mechanism. It also clarifies prior knowledge as a boundary condition of algorithm aversion in human-AI interaction.

items.title: Dual context attentive feature network: an interpretable dual-pathway deep learning framework for accurate gastrointestinal endoscopic image classification
items.abstract: Background: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases such as colorectal cancer and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) contribute substantially to global morbidity, with colorectal cancer accounting for nearly 10% of all cancer diagnoses worldwide. Many existing artificial intelligence (AI) models suffer from limited generalizability and poor clinical interpretability. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an explainable AI (XAI) framework for classifying GI diseases from endoscopic images. Methods: Public datasets from the Simula Research Laboratory were used: Hyper-Kvasir (10,662 images) for training, Kvasir-V1 (4,000 images) for validation, and Kvasir-V2 (8,000 images) as an independent test set. Two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, GastroNet-dilated multi-scale attention (DMSA) (a proposed DMSA Network) and M2ShallowNet (a lightweight hybrid model), were designed for complementary feature extraction. Deep features were fused using a dual context attentive feature network (DCAF-Net) followed by Aquila Optimizer (AO)-based feature-weight refinement without introducing additional trainable fusion parameters. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and statistical testing. Interpretability was examined using gradient-weighted class activation mapping++ (Grad-CAM++) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results: The best-performing classifier, a multilayer perceptron (MLP), achieved an accuracy of 97.21%, precision of 97.27%, recall of 97.21%, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 96.82%, and F1-score of 97.21% on the independent test set. ROC analysis demonstrated excellent class separability, and statistical testing confirmed reliable generalization. XAI results highlighted regions that qualitatively correspond to pathological areas; formal clinical validation of these interpretations was not performed in this study. Conclusions: The proposed framework offers a promising research prototype for AI-assisted GI disease classification. Its potential for real-world endoscopic deployment requires further prospective validation before clinical adoption.

items.title: Dynamics of collective creativity in AI art competitions
items.abstract: Abstract Creativity is a fundamental part of cultural evolution, but the mechanisms by which groups produce novelty are notoriously difficult to infer from the historical record. Iterated learning experiments have shown that cultural transmission reliably distorts artifacts toward the inductive biases of learners, but most of this work uses linear chains of human participants, and it is unclear how these dynamics play out in the networked, human-AI systems that increasingly shape cultural production. In this study, we analyze one such system: Artbreeder, which hosts daily “remix parties” in which users iteratively build on each other's work from a single seed image, producing branching lineages of images co-created by humans and generative AI. Using 130,882 images from 368 remix parties over 13 months, we find that images become less novel over the course of a party and that each remix step moves less far from its parents, consistent with the stabilization seen in iterated learning experiments, and that late-stage images drift toward the platform's dominant portrait style. More novel “parent” images produce more novel and more complex “children.” More novel children attract more likes but are not remixed more, whereas more complex children are remixed less. Finally, larger remix parties produce images that are more novel but less complex.

items.title: EBM-Nav: energy-based model for zero-shot visual navigation via implicit scene representation
items.abstract: Abstract Zero-shot visual navigation enables agents to generalize to unseen environments without task-specific training and is core to service robotics, warehouse logistics, and autonomous exploration. Existing approaches are observed to fail to achieve genuine zero-shot generalization: explicit-map methods rely on accurate reconstruction and are sensitive to sensor noise; supervised policies memorize training-scene patterns and degrade under illumination, furniture, and layout shifts; implicit representations offer continuous, differentiable encoding but remain confined to passive reconstruction and lack effective coupling with active decisions. To address this, EBM-Nav is proposed as a zero-shot navigation framework built on an energy-based model. Specifically, a periodic-activation implicit scene encoder is employed to map discrete RGB-D observations into a continuous, differentiable representation supporting arbitrary-resolution spatial queries. An energy function over the observation–action–goal triple is designed to reformulate navigation as gradient descent on an energy landscape. A frozen multimodal large language model is integrated to decompose long-horizon instructions into subgoals and generate candidate directions. A contrastive-divergence learning mechanism is developed with short-step Langevin dynamics to efficiently construct negative samples for training the energy function. Systematic experiments are conducted on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE continuous vision-and-language navigation benchmarks, and it is shown that EBM-Nav significantly outperforms state-of-the-art zero-shot methods in success rate, path efficiency, and navigation accuracy, while providing an interpretable energy-confidence mechanism for decisions. These results verify the energy-landscape zero-shot navigation paradigm, offer a general learning paradigm for embodied intelligence, and extend energy-based models from static perception to sequential decision-making, with methodological implications for service robots and autonomous exploration.

items.title: Effect of Trust in AI on Human AI Relationship among University Students
items.abstract: The study aimed to examine the effect of trust in AI on Human-AI relationship among university students. A cross-sectional survey research design was used. The sample comprised 300 university students (150 males and 150 females) selected through convenient sampling technique. Measures included the General Attitude toward AI Scale (GAAIS) by Schepman and Rodway (32 items, Positive α = .84, Negative α = .73), Short Trust in Automation Scale (S-TIAS) by McGrath et al. (3 items, α = .88), and Experiences in Human-AI Relationships Scale (EHARS) by Yang and Oshio (7 items). Correlation analysis showed that trust in AI was positively correlated with Human-AI relationship. The study contributed to the growing literature on Human-AI relationships by highlighting the role of trust in AI in Human-AI interactions among university students. The findings have important implications for AI literacy, technology acceptance, and the development of educational interventions aimed at fostering healthy and effective Human-AI relationships.

items.title: EFFECTS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) ON STUDENT PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS
items.abstract: This study determined the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted pedagogy on the problem-solving skills of first-year Bachelor of Secondary Education students enrolled in Mathematics in the Modern World at Urdaneta City University. The study was completed in May 2026 during School Year 2025-2026. Using a quasi-experimental pre-test and post-test non-equivalent group design, the researchers compared the performance of students taught through conventional pedagogy with those who experienced AI-supported instruction. Problem-solving performance was examined using George Pólya's four-step framework: understanding the problem, planning a solution, carrying out the plan, and checking the solution. Initial results showed that both groups had limited problem-solving skills before instruction, especially in planning, execution, and verification. After the intervention, both groups improved; however, students exposed to AI-assisted pedagogy obtained stronger gains, particularly in carrying out the plan and overall problem-solving performance. The paired-samples t-test indicated significant improvement within the experimental group, while the independent-samples t-test showed that the experimental group outperformed the conventional group in selected post-test measures. The findings suggest that AI tools, when used with teacher guidance and structured problem-solving activities, can support mathematical learning by offering immediate feedback, alternative explanations, and opportunities for solution checking. The study further indicates that AI should be integrated as a cognitive support rather than as a substitute for independent reasoning.

items.title: Emerging paradigm in sensor based pedology: Advances, applications, challenges and future perspectives
items.abstract: Pedology has seen a significant revolution due to the adoption of modern sensors that can provide fast, non-invasive and high resolution measurements of soils. Traditional pedological surveys that rely on field work and laboratory analysis are efficient, yet time consuming, cumbersome and have exhibit low spatial resolution. Modern advancements in sensors that measure optical, geophysical, elemental, moisture and remote sensing characteristics of soils have considerably improved the evaluation of soil’s physical, chemical and morphological characteristics. This article provides a detailed overview of emerging sensor-based techniques in pedology including the principles of these techniques, their applications and limitations. The review further examines the roles of digital soil mapping (DSM), proximal soil sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), machine learning and artificial intelligence in enhancing soil property prediction and spatial modelling. This review also highlights the significance of calibration and validation of sensors and ground truthing of observations. It critically analyses the problems associated with the calibration transferability, soil heterogeneity, moisture effects and cost of sensors. Recent advances in sensor fusion, internet of things (IoT)-enabled monitoring, hyperspectral imaging and explainable artificial intelligence are also discussed as promising directions for future soil assessment. Furthermore, major research gaps including the need for standardised calibration protocols, regional soil spectral libraries, affordable sensing technologies and interpretable machine-learning models are identified. Overall, sensor-based pedology complements conventional soil survey methods by providing accurate, efficient and spatially continuous soil information thereby supporting sustainable soil management, precision agriculture, environmental monitoring and evidence-based land-use planning under changing climatic conditions.

items.title: Emerging Technologies and Active Pedagogies in Initial Teacher Education: Preliminary Findings from a Systematic Review
items.abstract: Initial teacher education is under growing pressure to prepare future teachers for technology-rich classrooms and for pedagogical approaches that promote active student participation. This study presents preliminary findings from a systematic review examining how educational research addresses digital, emerging, and generative technologies in relation to the development of active pedagogies in initial teacher education. The review followed the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) protocol. Peer-reviewed articles published in English or Spanish between 2015 and June 2025 were retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and Dialnet using three search strings related to new technologies, generative artificial intelligence, and active pedagogies in initial teacher education. Eligible studies focused on pre-service teachers and teacher educators in European and Latin American contexts. After full screening, 66 articles were included. Preliminary findings indicate that literature pays considerable attention to technology integration in school settings, whereas fewer studies examine how initial teacher education programs prepare pre-service teachers to implement innovative pedagogies supported by emerging technologies. These findings point to a persistent misalignment between teacher education, emerging technologies, and active pedagogies, as technology is often approached as a technical resource rather than as a driver of pedagogical transformation. The study offers an updated overview of research trends and identifies a persistent gap in the preparation of future teachers for innovative classroom practice.

items.title: Empathy as an Aesthetic Infrastructure of Intercultural Communication: China and Post-Yugoslav Digital Narratives in the Age of AI
items.abstract: This article examines intercultural communication between China and the post-Yugoslav states in the context of globalization and the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), proposing empathy as a central yet ambivalent aesthetic infrastructure through which cultural difference is mediated. While digital platforms and AI technologies have dramatically increased the intensity and visibility of cross-cultural encounters, they have also transformed the conditions under which cultures are perceived, felt, and understood. Drawing on continental philosophy, moral psychology, and communication theory—particularly the work of Jean-Luc Nancy, Maurice Blanchot, Zygmunt Bauman, Martin Hoffman, and Jürgen Habermas—this study conceptualizes empathy not merely as a psychological or ethical capacity, but as an aesthetic and communicative form shaped by media technologies. Drawing on a theoretical-comparative and interpretative approach, the article examines Chinese and post-Yugoslav affective and aesthetic regimes as they are represented, circulated, and emotionally experienced within contemporary digital environments. Chinese culture is globally circulated through narratives of harmony, technological progress, and collective futurity, while post-Yugoslav cultures are framed through trauma, nostalgia, and emotional authenticity. These representations invite empathic engagement, yet often at the cost of historical depth, internal plurality, and ethical responsibility. The article argues that AI-driven empathy produces emotional proximity without genuine dialogue, replacing communicative understanding with affective optimization. In response, it proposes a critical aesthetics of empathic communication that preserves distance, opacity, and interpretive labor as necessary conditions for meaningful intercultural dialogue. Such an approach is essential for rethinking cultural exchange between China and the post-Yugoslav space in the age of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Energy Audits in Tanzanian Industrial SMEs for Methods, Barriers, and M&V-Linked Savings Prioritization
items.abstract: This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.

items.title: Energy Forecasting and Prediction Using Intelligent Controllers: AI-Driven Strategies for Microgrid Optimization
items.abstract: In this chapter, we introduce a solar irradiance prediction and forecasting method for microgrid optimization based on artificial intelligence (AI), which employs Global Tilted Irradiance (GTI) as a key input to improve the accuracy of photovoltaic (PV) power prediction. Unlike conventional irradiance indices, GTI aligns better with real-world setups, particularly due to its relevance for tilted solar panels. Based on historical data from Visakhapatnam, India, three machine learning models Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost were trained to predict GTI. CatBoost delivered the most accurate results, having the highest R 2 (0.9993) and lowest Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) (7.37). Furthermore, CatBoost was used to forecast GTI values that were connected to operational decision-making in batteries, loads, and grid interaction. These strategies were implemented in an Energy Management System (EMS) for automated control. The study demonstrates how GTI-based forecasting with intelligent controllers enhances microgrid performance, reliability, and sustainability.

items.title: Enhancing Cognitive Ergonomics in Robotic Surgery—A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) has transformed minimally invasive procedures by improving physical ergonomics, surgical field visualisation and instrument manipulation. However, RAS introduces unique cognitive load for the surgeon. Cognitive ergonomics aims to enhance the mental resources to optimise the interactions between surgeons and their environment, thereby improving the wellbeing and performance of surgeons and patient outcomes. Current evidence highlights that RAS redistributes, rather than eliminates, ergonomic burden from the physical to the mental domain. Subjective measurement tools remain the most widely used; however, physiological measures offer continuous and real-time data regarding cognitive workload fluctuations during surgery. Strategies to improve cognitive ergonomics include surgeon-level strategies, interface and system design alterations, operating room workflow optimisation, incorporation of artificial intelligence, and training and education. This narrative review summarises the current evidence regarding the mental demands associated with RAS, cognitive workload measures, the consequences of poor cognition, and emerging strategies to improve cognitive ergonomics in RAS.

items.title: Enhancing Democratic Listening in Online Discussions: The Role of Reaction Buttons, Discussion Moderation, and Large Language Models
items.abstract: Political communication research in general – and research on political online discussions in particular – has previously focused on the exercise of democratic voice and thus largely neglected the complementary practice of democratic listening. Against the backdrop of a wide-spread perception that democratic listening is lacking in online discussions, we investigate whether listening can be strengthened through novel platform affordances. We developed an experimental online written discussion platform with listening-oriented reaction buttons and both human and AI moderation (based on GPT-4). We then conducted an experiment involving n = 740 respondents in 40 discussion groups (N = 4,355 comments), each lasting 30 minutes, covering three experimental conditions and a control condition. We compare the effect of (1) listening-oriented reaction buttons versus (2) a combination of these buttons and listening-oriented human discussion moderation versus (3) a combination of buttons and AI moderation on the level of democratic listening demonstrated in discussants’ textual contributions. We find that listening-oriented buttons alone do not enhance democratic listening. However, when combined with listening-oriented AI moderation, they are associated with a democratic listening rate of 27% within discussions, compared to 21% in the condition without either feature. Our findings lay the basis for the implementation of a combination of listening-oriented buttons and discussion moderation on news media websites, social media apps or dedicated discussion spaces using LLM-based chatbots.

items.title: Enhancing Empathy in Nursing Students Through a Multimodal Artificial Intelligence-Supported Simulation: A Mixed-Methods Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Empathic communication is a core competency in nursing practice, yet providing nursing students with realistic opportunities to develop this competency remains challenging. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled the integration of behavioral and physiological data into simulation-based education. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of a multimodal AI-supported simulation in improving empathy, communication self-efficacy, and learning engagement among undergraduate nursing students. METHODS: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study was conducted with 134 undergraduate nursing students (68 experimental and 66 control). The experimental group received multimodal AI-supported simulation integrating conversational AI, facial emotion recognition, speech analysis, and physiological monitoring, whereas the control group received conventional role-play-based simulation with faculty-led debriefing. RESULTS: After adjustment for baseline scores, the experimental group showed significantly greater improvements in empathy, communication self-efficacy, and emotional, behavioral, and cognitive engagement than the control group (all P < .001). Heart rate variability and galvanic skin response showed significant group-by-time differences, indicating differential physiological responses during the simulation. Qualitative findings indicated enhanced empathy awareness, communication confidence, and reflective learning. CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal AI-supported simulation improved empathy, communication self-efficacy, and learning engagement by providing integrated behavioral and physiological feedback. This approach may serve as a complementary educational strategy to support empathic communication training in undergraduate nursing education.

items.title: Enhancing Large Language Models with External Knowledge Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Critical Review of Retrieval Design, Context Compression, Safety and Evaluation, with a Conceptual Governance-Aware Architecture
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) depend on static parametric knowledge, leading to outdated answers, missing expertise, and hallucinations. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses these issues by retrieving external evidence during inference, but the interactions between design choices are not well understood. This critical review explores configuration benchmarking, embedding quality, question-type-adaptive retrieval with context compression, comparison with fine-tuning, IAM-based permission filtering, and real-time, safety-critical graph-based RAG. A focused narrative design was used on a defined corpus, with foundational sources. The findings show that no single RAG configuration is best, as the optimal choice depends on the task and metrics. Retrieval quality strongly correlates with answer quality for extractive tasks but weakly for synthesis tasks. Adaptive retrieval and compression can reduce token usage but increase latency. Access control, freshness, and safety can be enforced outside the LLM, but this is only possible under explicit trust assumptions. However, most studies rely on Wikipedia-based question answering, small samples, single runs, and inconsistent metrics. Several studies also contain internal inconsistencies, which are documented here. This review contributes five key elements: a survey matrix, a comparative analysis that separates different experimental settings, an eight-layer conceptual architecture justified by literature, a minimum evaluation protocol for fair comparison, and a research gap agenda linked to evidence. These outputs provide researchers and practitioners with a foundation for building reliable, secure, and governable RAG systems in real-world, enterprise, and safety-critical applications.

items.title: Estereotipos Algorítmicos: Un Estudio Experimental sobre Sesgos de Género en la IA Generative
items.abstract: This study analyzes how citizens identify gender biases in narratives generated by artificial intelligence (AI), using ChatGPT as a case study. An online experiment was conducted with 614 Spanish participants, randomly assigned to three conditions: a professional success narrative featuring a female protagonist, a narrative featuring a male protagonist, and a neutral narrative. After exposure, gender bias detection in the story, perceived bias in ChatGPT, and the intention to reduce or correct algorithmic biases were measured. The results show that the narrative featuring a female protagonist was associated with higher bias detection and greater attribution of partiality to ChatGPT. No significant differences were observed according to participants’ gender or educational level. Likewise, indicators of proximity to AI, such as interest in these technologies and the use of AI-based applications, were associated with lower perceived bias in the tool. The findings underscore the need to promote critical AI literacy that helps citizens more critically recognize when its outputs reproduce gender stereotypes or inequalities.

items.title: Ethical and Legal Dimensions of AI in Digital Forensics and Cybersecurity
items.abstract: The use of technology to gather, store, examine, and display digital evidence in accordance with a set of regulations is known as digital forensics. According to Cyber, the variety of cyberattitudes is altering people’s perceptions of cybercrime in a distinctive manner. This facilitates the acquisition of digital evidence and the handling of digital content. Due to the increasing prevalence of cyber dangers in the digital environment, “manual” forensic investigations are rapidly becoming obsolete. Most people whose job it is to locate digital evidence have recently been affected by this critical predicament. It cannot advance by using fresh strategies and tactics. To address this demand, it must develop new methods and instruments as fast and precisely as it did before. Artificial intelligence, deep learning, machine learning, and the development of natural human language have all contributed to significant change. Every cybersecurity and digital forensics specialist in the world might benefit from these new tools and systems, which could also alter how they do their duties.

items.title: Ethical Considerations in AI-Driven Travel Management Systems
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into travel management systems presents profound ethical challenges that demand systematic examination. This chapter investigates the multifaceted ethical dimensions arising from AI deployment in travel management, encompassing algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, human agency, environmental sustainability, and equity of access. Drawing on recent scholarship in AI ethics, information systems, and tourism studies, the chapter argues that uncritical adoption of AI in travel management risks entrenching discrimination, eroding traveller autonomy, and exacerbating socioeconomic divides. The chapter proposes a normative framework grounded in fairness, accountability, and sustainability principles to guide responsible AI deployment. Recommendations for practitioners, policymakers, and technology developers are provided to ensure that AI-driven travel systems serve human flourishing and inclusive progress.

items.title: Evaluating Locally Grounded Generative AI for Health-Policy Support: A Multilevel Mixed-Methods Pilot Study
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may assist evidence-informed health-policy work, but favorable user perceptions and well-written outputs do not establish factual reliability or implementation readiness. A multilevel mixed-methods pilot evaluation examined MUSYA AI, a locally grounded policy-support platform in Thailand. Thirty-five health-sector personnel completed questionnaires, seven participated in Think-Aloud observation, sixteen Policy Briefs were assessed using an expert rubric, and seventy factual claims underwent evidence auditing. The document comparison included eight MUSYA AI and eight ChatGPT (GPT-5.6, OpenAI) outputs under common task instructions and system-specific information access. Mean System Usability Scale, perceived usefulness, and trust scores were 97.29/100, 4.70/5, and 4.57/5, respectively. Ceiling effects and limited internal consistency constrained interpretation of these descriptive indices; user experience, ease of use, and behavioral intention were interpreted at the item level. Observations documented reading and editing, but successful error detection and correction were not evaluated. MUSYA AI documents received higher overall quality ratings than comparator documents (95.38 ± 2.39 versus 72.25 ± 11.90; difference, 23.13 points; bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 15.63–31.38; Hedges’ g = 2.55). However, classification–rationale inconsistencies affected forty-five claims (64.3%), leaving comparative factual-accuracy findings provisional. The small, nonrandomized document sample and absence of verified task pairing prevented causal attribution of quality differences. MUSYA AI elicited favorable pilot-user perceptions and produced higher-rated documents within the evaluated sample. These findings support continued supervised evaluation; institutional readiness requires traceable claim adjudication, demonstrated oversight effectiveness, and broader controlled assessment.

items.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of AI-Based adaptive learning for reading development and self-regulated learning among pupils with dyslexia in Abuja, Nigeria
items.abstract: Children with dyslexia often experience persistent challenges in reading, motivation, and self-regulation within traditional classroom settings that rely on uniform instructional approaches. With the growing integration of artificial intelligence in education, AI-based adaptive learning systems have emerged as innovative tools capable of personalizing instruction and supporting diverse learning needs. This study investigated the effect of AI-based adaptive learning systems on reading performance, motivation, and self-regulation among primary school students with dyslexia in Abuja, Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design was adopted, with a sample of 60 Primary 5 pupils drawn from selected inclusive and special education schools in the Abuja Municipal Area. Data were collected using a Reading Performance Test, Motivation toward Reading Scale, and Self-Regulation in Reading Questionnaire, and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including independent samples t-test. Findings revealed that students exposed to AI-based adaptive learning demonstrated significantly higher improvements across all variables compared to those receiving conventional instruction. The experimental group recorded substantial gains in reading performance (mean gain = 24.20), motivation (mean gain = 1.50), and self-regulation (mean gain = 1.60), compared to the control group. Statistical analysis confirmed that these differences were significant (p < 0.05). These findings align with Cognitive Load Theory, Self-Determination Theory, and Vygotsky’s Zone of Proximal Development. The study concludes that AI-based adaptive learning systems offer an effective approach for improving both academic and psychological outcomes among students with dyslexia. It recommends the integration of AI-driven instructional tools in primary education, alongside teacher training and policy support, to promote inclusive, personalized, and effective learning environments.

items.title: EVALUATION OF INTERNAL CONTROLS OVER THE REVENUE CYCLE: A CASE STUDY OF RETAIL COMPANY X
items.abstract: This study evaluates internal controls over the revenue cycle at Retail X, a modern convenience store chain operating a digital ordering application integrated with a Point of Sale (POS) system. The evaluation applies the COSO Internal Control–Integrated Framework/ICIF (COSO, 2013), focusing on two components: Risk Assessment and Control Activities. A descriptive case study approach was employed, with data collected through semi-structured interviews with three informants—the Store Manager, Cashier, and Service Crew—and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings identify four operational risks: transaction input errors, product preparation errors, order pickup errors, and disruptions in receiving digital orders. These risks stem from employee-customer-system interactions and limitations in human resources and digital infrastructure. Control activities implemented include order confirmation, preparation SOPs, order labeling, product remaking, and manual order verification. However, the evaluation reveals uneven control coverage, heavy reliance on human factors, and a predominance of corrective over preventive controls. By tracing risk from its source to the adequacy of existing controls, this study extends the application of COSO ICIF to digitally integrated retail settings in developing economies. The study concludes that strengthening internal control requires procedural improvements alongside enhanced human resource capacity and information system infrastructure.

items.title: Evidence-Grounded Autonomous Web Application Testing: A Scope-Aware Framework for Reliable AI-Generated QA Reports
items.abstract: Abstract Autonomous artificial intelligence agents powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for web application testing, usability evaluation, and software quality assurance. However, significant challenges remain in ensuring reliable defect detection, comprehensive test coverage, reproducible findings, and evidence-based reporting. This working paper introduces Evidence-Grounded Autonomous Quality Assurance (EG-AQA), a proposed framework for improving the transparency, reliability, and reproducibility of AI-generated web application testing reports. The framework combines task-oriented browser exploration, structured evidence collection, independent verification mechanisms, explicit testing-scope accounting, and uncertainty-aware reporting. The research examines how autonomous testing systems can distinguish verified software defects from unsupported interpretations, incomplete observations, environmental restrictions, and issues requiring human judgment. It also proposes quantitative evaluation methods for measuring defect-detection precision and recall, navigation coverage, task completion, finding reproducibility, and computational efficiency. The study uses an anonymized, limited observation from an early-stage Cohorvix testing report to illustrate challenges associated with incomplete exploration and the interpretation of automated testing evidence. A reproducible experimental methodology is proposed for future validation using controlled web applications, independently documented defects, repeated testing sessions, comparative baselines, and human adjudication. The paper contributes a structured research framework and evaluation protocol intended to support more accountable and evidence-grounded AI-powered website testing. The proposed improvements have not yet been validated through a completed comparative experiment. Publication status: Research working paper, Version 1.0. items.title: Evidence-Grounded SLM Behavioral Prediction Architecture for Future Assistance Use
items.abstract: Users often exhibit changes in interaction behavior before explicitly seeking assistance, enabling systems to anticipate future assistance use. This is especially important in high-stakes environments, where delayed assistance can have operational, financial, or safety consequences. However, conventional Large Language Models (LLMs) are often unsuitable for continuous on-device behavioral prediction because of their computational and memory demands. Behavioral patterns are also highly individual and device-specific, motivating local processing that preserves privacy and data sovereignty. Small Language Models (SLMs) offer a promising alternative, but their ability to reason reliably over low-level sequential interaction events remains underexplored. This study introduces Evidence-Grounded Local Behavioral Prediction (ELBP), a four-layer architecture combining deterministic interaction processing, dual-view behavioral representation, SLM-based prediction, and evidence verification with abstention. Three instruction-tuned models of 3B parameters or fewer were evaluated using raw, structured, dual-view, and complete ELBP configurations. The best-performing model, Qwen2.5-3B with ELBP, achieved a full-set F1-score of 0.80 and PR-AUC of 0.84, representing a 15.9\% relative improvement over raw-event prompting and 17.6\% over XGBoost, while full-set ECE decreased by 43.2\% relative to raw-event prompting. With evidence verification and abstention, selective F1 increased to 0.84 at 91\% coverage and evidence support reached 96\%. These results show that structured behavioral representation and evidence-verified selective prediction can improve the reliability of behavioral forecasting in SLMs.

items.title: Evolution of Aggregation-Induced Emission Materials in Cancer Diagnosis and Therapy: Toward Clinical Translation
items.abstract: Conspectus As one of the most formidable threats to human health, cancer demands technologies that can sensitively detect malignancies, precisely guide intervention, adapt to dynamic disease states, and support clinical decision-making. Phototheranostics based on organic fluorophores have shown great promise in cancer management owing to their tunable structural design, tumor-targeting capability, real-time imaging output, and biocompatibility with diverse therapeutic modalities. However, conventional fluorophores often suffer from aggregation-caused quenching in concentrated or biological aggregate states, leading to weakened signals, insufficient sensitivity, and limited therapeutic efficacy. The discovery of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) provides a conceptually distinct solution to this problem. AIE materials are weakly emissive in the molecularly dispersed state but become highly luminescent upon aggregation, thereby turning aggregation from a detrimental process into a useful photophysical mechanism. By precisely controlling molecular motion, AIE materials can exhibit advantages including high signal-to-noise ratio, large Stokes shifts, and excellent photostability, making them a versatile molecular toolbox for tumor-oriented phototheranostic systems. Over the past two decades, they have evolved beyond simple fluorescent probes into integrated platforms for cancer theranostics. In this Account, we propose a concept-driven framework, termed AIMS (Analyze-Intervene-Modulate-Select), to organize the evolution of AIE materials in cancer diagnosis and therapy according to their distinctive roles within cancer management. The first generation, “Analyze”, refers to AIE materials used mainly as diagnostic tools. These systems enable sensitive detection of tumor-associated biomarkers, in vivo lesion visualization, and multimodal intraoperative identification. The second generation, “Intervene”, generates all-in-one theranostic platforms that couple imaging with phototherapy, facilitating radiotherapy sensitization, immune activation, or postoperative control. The third generation, “Modulate”, describes intelligent and adaptive AIE platforms that respond to therapy-induced stress, microenvironmental shifts, or dynamic biological feedback during treatment, transforming static theranostics into systems capable of modulating therapeutic trajectories. The emerging fourth generation, “Select”, represents a data-driven paradigm linking the design of AIE materials with artificial intelligence, multiomics, patient stratification, model selection, and indication prioritization. Through AIMS, we organize the accumulated capabilities of AIE materials around four functional roles. By clarifying which role is most relevant to a given application, AIMS guides future research in prioritizing design objectives, integrating the functions needed for the intended task, and matching material innovation to specific needs in cancer management.

items.title: Explainable AI and Real-Time Decisioning for Automated Government Case Management in Saudi Arabia
items.abstract: Automated government case management is moving from digitised workflow toward intelligent triage, eligibility assessment, risk prioritisation and service routing. In Saudi Arabia, this transition is especially consequential because digital government programmes increasingly connect high-volume public services with data-intensive decision processes. The central challenge is not simply whether artificial intelligence can accelerate case handling, but whether decisions can remain timely, reviewable, understandable and contestable when models operate at operational speed. This review examines how explainable artificial intelligence and real-time decisioning can be combined for automated government case management in Saudi Arabia. It synthesises thirty DOI-verified studies published from 2020 to 2025 across explainability, human-AI decision support, public-sector algorithmic governance, Saudi digital government and streaming analytics. The review develops a socio-technical framework in which case intake, data quality, machine reasoning, rule validation, explanation generation, human oversight, notification, appeal and continuous monitoring form one auditable decision loop. The analysis finds that explainability is valuable only when it is matched to the decision recipient and linked to operational controls; generic feature-attribution displays alone do not guarantee justified or trustworthy outcomes. Real-time systems also require explicit latency budgets, uncertainty handling, concept-drift monitoring and escalation rules so that speed does not suppress due process. For Saudi public agencies, successful adoption depends on combining interoperable data, secure governance, accountable ownership and Arabic-capable explanation interfaces with measurable human override and appeal mechanisms. The study proposes evaluation criteria spanning predictive validity, explanation fidelity, decision latency, fairness, reviewability and institutional accountability. It concludes that explainable real-time case management should be designed as governed decision infrastructure rather than as an isolated prediction model.

items.title: Explainable AI in Neural Poetry Generation: Beyond Attention
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is increasingly important for ensuring transparency and trust in neural systems; however, its applicability to creative text generation remains limited. Neural poetry generation models produce linguistically coherent and stylistically rich outputs, yet explaining decisions such as metaphor construction, emotional tone, and thematic development remains unresolved. This systematic literature review synthesizes 26 peer‐reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a predefined protocol across four major digital libraries. The analysis identifies a fundamental mismatch between existing XAI paradigms and the properties of generative modeling. We propose a taxonomy distinguishing classification‐native methods from generation‐compatible approaches, highlighting their differing assumptions. Based on established criteria of contrastivity, selectivity, and faithfulness, we show that attention mechanisms lack causal validity as explanatory tools. To consolidate these findings, we introduce a unified failure framework comprising five interacting structural limitations: token–semantic mismatch, attention non‐causality, classification–generation incompatibility, evaluation collapse, and human–model ontological misalignment. These limitations collectively constrain the effectiveness of current XAI methods in creative contexts. Our findings indicate that advancing explainability in neural poetry generation requires a shift toward semantic‐level representations, causal intervention‐based approaches, and human‐centered evaluation frameworks that incorporate aesthetic and interpretive dimensions.
